name: Stratos Project Ruby Pipeline Lateral
monitor_reason: no pipeline project described: sources say the campus would use unused capacity on the existing Ruby Pipeline, which crosses the site, and none describes a new lateral, supply line or named tap. It would become a project when a Tallgrass or Ruby filing, a Utah air permit application, a development agreement text, or a developer or county document says a line or connection will be built to the campus.
researcher_notes: This was re-checked under the 2026-10-19 ruling. Location, sponsor and length are no longer required, but a pipeline project still has to be described. None is. A Box Elder County fact sheet lists direct access to the Ruby Pipeline as a selling point of the site. A WyoFile story from May 2026 quotes the developer's co-founder at an April 27 county meeting saying the data center would tap unused capacity on the pipeline that is not under contract. That is use of existing capacity, not new pipe. A Pipeline and Gas Journal story from May 2026 says Ruby is eyed for the project, but its text could not be read past the headline. Third-party listings and press say gas would come through a Tallgrass deal and a connection to Ruby, but none describes a lateral or names a tap, and no Tallgrass notice, federal filing or Utah air permit application was found. A tap or meter station with no new pipe is only added when a filing names it. Do not tag the Ruby Pipeline row (P0248). Earlier work on this lead (Landgate article, ABC4 development agreement documents) is unchanged.
